# `/configuration-hub` endpoints

Base URL: `https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com`

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/object-mappings/{sourceOrg}

`getObjectMappingsV1` — Gets list of object mappings

This gets a list of existing object mappings between current org and source org. Source org should be "default" when getting object mappings that are not associated to any particular org. The request will need the following security scope: - sp:config-object-mapping:read

- Scopes: sp:config-object-mapping:manage, sp:config-object-mapping:read
- Parameters:
  - `sourceOrg` (path, required) — The name of the source org.
- Returns 200: array of objectmappingresponse

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/object-mappings/{sourceOrg}

`createObjectMappingV1` — Creates an object mapping

This creates an object mapping between current org and source org. Source org should be "default" when creating an object mapping that is not to be associated to any particular org. The request will need the following security scope: - sp:config-object-mapping:manage

- Scopes: sp:config-object-mapping:manage
- Parameters:
  - `sourceOrg` (path, required) — The name of the source org.
- Body (application/json): objectmappingrequest
- Returns 200: objectmappingresponse

### DELETE /configuration-hub/v1/object-mappings/{sourceOrg}/{objectMappingId}

`deleteObjectMappingV1` — Deletes an object mapping

This deletes an existing object mapping. Source org should be "default" when deleting an object mapping that is not associated to any particular org. The request will need the following security scope: - sp:config-object-mapping:manage

- Scopes: sp:config-object-mapping:manage
- Parameters:
  - `sourceOrg` (path, required) — The name of the source org.
  - `objectMappingId` (path, required) — The id of the object mapping to be deleted.
- Returns 204: no body

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/object-mappings/{sourceOrg}/bulk-create

`createObjectMappingsV1` — Bulk creates object mappings

This creates a set of object mappings (Max 25) between current org and source org. Source org should be "default" when creating object mappings that are not to be associated to any particular org. The request will need the following security scope: - sp:config-object-mapping:manage

- Scopes: sp:config-object-mapping:manage
- Parameters:
  - `sourceOrg` (path, required) — The name of the source org.
- Body (application/json): objectmappingbulkcreaterequest
- Returns 200: objectmappingbulkcreateresponse

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/object-mappings/{sourceOrg}/bulk-patch

`updateObjectMappingsV1` — Bulk updates object mappings

This updates a set of object mappings, only enabled and targetValue fields can be updated. Source org should be "default" when updating object mappings that are not associated to any particular org. The request will need the following security scope: - sp:config-object-mapping:manage

- Scopes: sp:config-object-mapping:manage
- Parameters:
  - `sourceOrg` (path, required) — The name of the source org.
- Body (application/json): objectmappingbulkpatchrequest
- Returns 200: objectmappingbulkpatchresponse

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/scheduled-actions

`listScheduledActionsV1` — List scheduled actions

This API gets a list of existing scheduled actions for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-scheduled-action:manage, sp:config-scheduled-action:read
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Returns 200: array of scheduledactionresponse

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/scheduled-actions

`createScheduledActionV1` — Create scheduled action

This API creates a new scheduled action for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-scheduled-action:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Body (application/json): scheduledactionpayload
- Returns 200: scheduledactionresponse

### PATCH /configuration-hub/v1/scheduled-actions/{id}

`updateScheduledActionV1` — Update scheduled action

This API updates an existing scheduled action using JSON Patch format.

- Scopes: sp:config-scheduled-action:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The ID of the scheduled action.
- Body (application/json-patch+json): jsonpatch
- Returns 200: scheduledactionresponse

### DELETE /configuration-hub/v1/scheduled-actions/{id}

`deleteScheduledActionV1` — Delete scheduled action

This API deletes an existing scheduled action.

- Scopes: sp:config-scheduled-action:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The ID of the scheduled action.
- Returns 204: no body

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/backups/uploads

`listUploadedConfigurationsV1` — List uploaded configurations

This API gets a list of existing uploaded configurations for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage, sp:config-backup:read
- Parameters:
  - `filters` (query) — fields: status: eq — e.g. `status eq "COMPLETE"`
- Returns 200: array of backupresponse

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/backups/uploads

`createUploadedConfigurationV1` — Upload a configuration

This API uploads a JSON configuration file into a tenant. Configuration files can be managed and deployed via Configuration Hub by uploading a json file which contains configuration data. The JSON file should be the same as the one used by our import endpoints. The object types supported by upload configuration file functionality are the same as the ones supported by our regular backup functionality. Refer to [SaaS…

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage
- Body (multipart/form-data): object
- Returns 202: backupresponse

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/backups/uploads/{id}

`getUploadedConfigurationV1` — Get an uploaded configuration

This API gets an existing uploaded configuration for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage, sp:config-backup:read
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The id of the uploaded configuration.
- Returns 200: backupresponse

### DELETE /configuration-hub/v1/backups/uploads/{id}

`deleteUploadedConfigurationV1` — Delete an uploaded configuration

This API deletes an uploaded configuration based on Id. On success, this endpoint will return an empty response. The uploaded configuration id can be obtained from the response after a successful upload, or the list uploaded configurations endpoint.

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The id of the uploaded configuration.
- Returns 204: no body

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/backups

`listBackupsV1` — List backups

This API gets a list of existing backups for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage, sp:config-backup:read
- Parameters:
  - `filters` (query) — fields: status: eq — e.g. `status eq "COMPLETE"`
- Returns 200: array of backupresponse

### DELETE /configuration-hub/v1/backups/{id}

`deleteBackupV1` — Delete a backup

This API deletes an existing backup for the current tenant. On success, this endpoint will return an empty response. The backup id can be obtained from the response after a backup was successfully created, or from the list backups endpoint.

- Scopes: sp:config-backup:manage
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The id of the backup to delete.
- Returns 204: no body

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/drafts

`listDraftsV1` — List drafts

This API gets a list of existing drafts for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-draft:manage, sp:config-draft:read
- Parameters:
  - `filters` (query) — fields: status: eq; approvalStatus: eq — e.g. `status eq "COMPLETE"`
- Returns 200: array of draftresponse

### DELETE /configuration-hub/v1/drafts/{id}

`deleteDraftV1` — Delete a draft

This API deletes an existing draft for the current tenant. On success, this endpoint will return an empty response. The draft id can be obtained from the response after a draft was successfully created, or from the list drafts endpoint.

- Scopes: sp:config-draft:manage
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The id of the draft to delete.
- Returns 204: no body

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/deploys

`listDeploysV1` — List deploys

This API gets a list of deploys for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-deploy:manage, sp:config-deploy:read
- Returns 200: object

### POST /configuration-hub/v1/deploys

`createDeployV1` — Create a deploy

This API performs a deploy based on an existing daft.

- Scopes: sp:config-deploy:manage
- Body (application/json): deployrequest
- Returns 202: deployresponse

### GET /configuration-hub/v1/deploys/{id}

`getDeployV1` — Get a deploy

This API gets an existing deploy for the current tenant.

- Scopes: sp:config-deploy:manage, sp:config-deploy:read
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The id of the deploy.
- Returns 200: deployresponse
